lines.say: This week, a report said Russia wants Finland out of NATO and a ban on military bases in the Baltics, as part of the Ukraine talks.
But in 1939, Moscow made demands of Finland too, and it ended in war.
In autumn 1939, the Soviet Union demanded that Finland push its border back and give up land for Soviet bases. Finland refused.
On November 30th, Soviet bombers hit Helsinki and the Red Army invaded.
Outnumbered, Finland's soldiers fought on through one of the coldest winters in memory.
They captured Soviet tanks, and held the Red Army for more than three months.
In March, Finland signed a peace and gave up a tenth of its land. But it stayed independent.
Now Finland is a NATO member, and Moscow wants that undone.
Should Moscow have a say in who Finland allies with?
